\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اجداد} (ajdād)}{اجداد (ajdād)}]{\ur{اجداد} (ajdād) — ancestors}

\label{lesson:UR-C315-ajdad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an inscription, then the Urdu for ancient remains.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اجداد}}
\textbf{\ur{اجداد}} — \emph{ajdād} — \textquotedblleft{}ancestors\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہمارے} \ur{اجداد} \ur{کسان} \ur{تھے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hamāre ajdād kisān the.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our ancestors were farmers.
\end{quote}

Masculine, used in the plural.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اجداد}} (\emph{ajdād}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ajdād}, the plural of \emph{jadd}, \textquotedblleft{}a grandfather\textquotedblright{}: the grandfathers of the grandfathers.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ajdād}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ajdād}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hamāre ajdād kisān the.} — Our ancestors were farmers.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for an inscription, then the Urdu for ancient remains, then say \emph{ajdād} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{اجداد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Ancestors\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بسنا} (basnā)}{بسنا (basnā)}]{\ur{بسنا} (basnā) — to settle; to make a home}

\label{lesson:UR-C315-basna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for ancient remains, then the Urdu for ancestors.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بسنا}}
\textbf{\ur{بسنا}} — \emph{basnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to settle; to make a home\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{دریا} \ur{کے} \ur{کنارے} \ur{بس} \ur{گئے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh daryā ke kināre bas gae.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They settled on the bank of the river.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{یہاں} \ur{بس} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh yahāṅ bas gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بسنا}} (\emph{basnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{basnā}, \textquotedblleft{}dwells\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{vásati} (CDIAL 11435). \textbf{\ur{بستی}}, a settlement, belongs with it.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نسل} (nasl)}{نسل (nasl)}]{\ur{نسل} (nasl) — a generation; a line of descent}

\label{lesson:UR-C315-nasl}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for ancestors, then the Urdu for to settle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نسل}}
\textbf{\ur{نسل}} — \emph{nasl} — \textquotedblleft{}a generation; a line of descent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہر} \ur{نسل} \ur{نے} \ur{یہ} \ur{گھر} \ur{سنبھالا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{har nasl ne yih ghar sambhālā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Every generation looked after this house.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{نسل}} (\emph{nasl}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{nasl}, \textquotedblleft{}offspring, descendants\textquotedblright{}. It is feminine: \textbf{\ur{نئی} \ur{نسل}}, the young generation.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\label{lesson:UR-C315-sadi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to settle, then the Urdu for a generation.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اجڑنا} (ujaṛnā)}{اجڑنا (ujaṛnā)}]{\ur{اجڑنا} (ujaṛnā) — to be ruined; to become deserted}

\label{lesson:UR-C315-ujarna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a generation, then the Urdu for a century.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اجڑنا}}
\textbf{\ur{اجڑنا}} — \emph{ujaṛnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to be ruined; to become deserted\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سیلاب} \ur{کے} \ur{بعد} \ur{گاؤں} \ur{اجڑ} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sailāb ke bād gāoṅ ujaṛ gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After the flood the village was left deserted.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{شہر} \ur{اجڑ} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh shahr ujaṛ gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اجڑنا}} (\emph{ujaṛnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ujaṛnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be uprooted\textquotedblright{}, under a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 1661). A place \textbf{\ur{اجڑ} \ur{گیا}} when its people left or were driven out.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Kings and Emperors to Ancestors}

\label{lesson:UR-R315-review-308-315}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for an emperor and a throne.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item an emperor, a throne, a crown, a royal court, an heir
  \item an attack, a fort, to surround, a cannon, to clash
  \item a sword, a shield, a spear, a bow for arrows, an army on the march
  \item to defeat, to throw down, a victory, a martyr, a peace settlement
  \item the subjects (of a ruler), an order, a slave, a rebellion, to challenge
  \item an English person, a movement (of people), a struggle, a sacrifice, to entrust
  \item ruins, to dig, a statue, an inscription, ancient remains
  \item ancestors, to settle, a generation, a century, to become deserted
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
An emperor? (\textbf{\ur{شہنشاہ}}, \emph{shahanshāh}.) A throne? (\textbf{\ur{تخت}}, \emph{takht}.) A crown? (\textbf{\ur{تاج}}, \emph{tāj}.) A royal court? (\textbf{\ur{دربار}}, \emph{darbār}.) An heir? (\textbf{\ur{وارث}}, \emph{vāris}.) An attack? (\textbf{\ur{حملہ}}, \emph{hamlā}.) A fort? (\textbf{\ur{قلعہ}}, \emph{qilā}.) To surround? (\textbf{\ur{گھیرنا}}, \emph{ghernā}.) A cannon? (\textbf{\ur{توپ}}, \emph{top}.) To clash? (\textbf{\ur{بھڑنا}}, \emph{bhiṛnā}.) A sword? (\textbf{\ur{تلوار}}, \emph{talvār}.) A shield? (\textbf{\ur{ڈھال}}, \emph{ḍhāl}.) A spear? (\textbf{\ur{بھالا}}, \emph{bhālā}.) A bow for arrows? (\textbf{\ur{کمان}}, \emph{kamān}.) An army on the march? (\textbf{\ur{لشکر}}, \emph{lashkar}.) To defeat? (\textbf{\ur{ہرانا}}, \emph{harānā}.) To throw down? (\textbf{\ur{پچھاڑنا}}, \emph{pachhāṛnā}.) A victory? (\textbf{\ur{فتح}}, \emph{fateh}.) A martyr? (\textbf{\ur{شہید}}, \emph{shahīd}.) A peace settlement? (\textbf{\ur{صلح}}, \emph{sulah}.) The subjects (of a ruler)? (\textbf{\ur{رعایا}}, \emph{riāyā}.) An order? (\textbf{\ur{حکم}}, \emph{hukm}.) A slave? (\textbf{\ur{غلام}}, \emph{ghulām}.) A rebellion? (\textbf{\ur{بغاوت}}, \emph{baghāvat}.) To challenge? (\textbf{\ur{للکارنا}}, \emph{lalkārnā}.) An English person? (\textbf{\ur{انگریز}}, \emph{angrez}.) A movement (of people)? (\textbf{\ur{تحریک}}, \emph{tahrīk}.) A struggle? (\textbf{\ur{جدوجہد}}, \emph{jaddojahd}.) A sacrifice? (\textbf{\ur{قربانی}}, \emph{qurbānī}.) To entrust? (\textbf{\ur{سونپنا}}, \emph{saunpnā}.) Ruins? (\textbf{\ur{کھنڈر}}, \emph{khanḍar}.) To dig? (\textbf{\ur{کھودنا}}, \emph{khodnā}.) A statue? (\textbf{\ur{مجسمہ}}, \emph{mujassamā}.) An inscription? (\textbf{\ur{کتبہ}}, \emph{katbā}.) Ancient remains? (\textbf{\ur{آثار}}, \emph{āsār}.) Ancestors? (\textbf{\ur{اجداد}}, \emph{ajdād}.) To settle? (\textbf{\ur{بسنا}}, \emph{basnā}.) A generation? (\textbf{\ur{نسل}}, \emph{nasl}.) A century? (\textbf{\ur{صدی}}, \emph{sadī}.) To become deserted? (\textbf{\ur{اجڑنا}}, \emph{ujaṛnā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
